children: Paramount Skydance wants plaintiffs in two antitrust lawsuits seeking to block its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery to post a bond to protect against its legal costs if the entertainment giant wins in court.

The company on Tuesday said it had satisfied all the closing conditions and received regulatory approvals for the merger, making the two lawsuits--one from a coalition of state attorneys general and the other from the Writers Guild of America--the only barrier to the merger.
Paramount also noted that it already agreed to delay the close of the deal to facilitate a speedy trial.

"If plaintiffs insist that this transaction is paused during the pendency of their lawsuit, they must accept the financial consequences if their challenge ultimately fails," a Paramount spokesperson said. "We are not asking the district court to lift the no-close order, but to require enforcement of the bond that protects our financial interests while the litigation remains pending."

The spokesperson added that the company would incur "substantial and quantifiable" costs from delaying the deal, and the federal antitrust laws "provide for a bond precisely to protect against exactly those types of losses if a court determines an injunction ultimately is unwarranted."
